flagged.title: Norman conquest and feudal warfare 1066-1215
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims on screen and in audio that King John lost Normandy at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214, when Normandy was lost in 1204 and Bouvines merely ended his attempt to regain it.

mark_affecting.quote: He lost the ancestral lands of Normandy at the Battle of Bouvines in 1214.

flagged.title: Elizabeth, Spain and the new world
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly locates the fireship attack at Gravelines instead of Calais and claims storms wrecked two-thirds of the fleet (contradicting the actual loss of around 50 of 130 ships), both of which are mark-affecting errors for GCSE students.

mark_affecting.quote: Fireships at Gravelines caused panic. / when the Spanish eventually anchored at Gravelines, the English sent in burning fireships
Severe storms wrecked two-thirds of the fleet. / storms that wrecked roughly two-thirds of their entire fleet

flagged.title: Border warfare c.1500-c.1600
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Henry VIII was fighting in Italy against the French in 1513, which would cause a student to lose marks when explaining the strategic context of the Auld Alliance and the causes of the Battle of Flodden.

mark_affecting.quote: That was triggered exactly because Henry VIII was busy fighting in Italy against the French
